approach: CP1 only: a new server/parser_probe.py holds all parser detection (same-install check, reflective ParserCore member probe, hc + GenerateHCConfig discovery, HC-agent probe, check_active_parser), composed by diagnostic_health.py into a new per-spine 'parser' health block. flextools_grammar_health ships the pure-LCM 9.5.4 static scan via the existing generated-module subprocess harness, since the MCP server process never opens a FieldWorks project. Four additive error codes join tool-responses/1.0.

decisions.decision: flextools_grammar_health runs its LCM scan in the generated-module subprocess via the existing execution.py harness
decisions.why: The MCP server process never opens a FieldWorks project -- every OpenProject lives in the script text execution.py generates. run_script_async kills the process tree on timeout so a wedged pythonnet child cannot hold the .fwdata lock; opening a project in the long-lived server process would defeat that.
decisions.rejected: Opening an LcmCache in the server process, or adding a third execution path just for read-only scans

decisions.decision: The ParserCore capability probe runs in-process in parser_probe.py, with call-site memoization
decisions.why: SPEC 5.4 requires the probe to never open an LcmCache. Assembly.LoadFile + member inspection is the pattern versioning.py:262 and liblcm_extractor.py:332 already use, and get_resolved_fieldworks_dir() already exists to bind it to the same FieldWorks install.
decisions.rejected: A module-level cache in parser_probe.py, which would need an invalidation policy versioning.py deliberately avoids

decisions.decision: In flextools_health the HC-agent probe always reports agent_probe=skipped; the probe itself ships as a reusable function for CP2 callers
decisions.why: SPEC 10.2 conditions the agent probe on a project being open, which the health handler can never reach. diagnostic_health.py is contractually pure composition and promises never to open a project. The spec already rules this state safe: skipped, not failed, and never reported as a pass.
decisions.rejected: Having health spawn a project-opening subprocess, or reporting write:unavailable when the probe cannot run

decisions.decision: SPEC 9.5.4 row 8 mapping is refuted and needs correction: rule ordering is not a property of IMoStratum
decisions.why: IMoStratum exposes exactly four own properties (Abbreviation, Description, Name, PhonemesRA) and no rule collection. Order lives on the rule: IPhSegmentRule.OrderNumber with InitialStratumRA/FinalStratumRA pointing rule->stratum. Also found: IPhSegmentRule.Disabled must gate every rule-based check, and IMoForm.IsComplete is a better row-6 predicate.
decisions.rejected: Writing row 8 as specified, which would look for a collection that does not exist

decisions.decision: Row 1 measured wording in contracts/flextools_grammar_health.md changed from "3 allomorphs with an empty surface form are reachable from an optional slot" to "3 allomorphs have an empty surface form", with a note explaining the CP1/CP2 split.
decisions.why: T033 found the contract example claimed slot-conditioning that CP1 does not measure -- the slot-reachability walk is deferred behind a known flexicon read gap (research D5/S9). Leaving it would have made the contract example itself violate T034s constraint that measured wording must not claim slot-conditioning, and would likely have failed T014s factual-phrasing assertion.
decisions.rejected: Leaving the contract example alone and letting T034 diverge from it, which would have made the contract untrustworthy as the assertion target.

plan.summary: CP1 plan + research + data-model + 3 contracts written; scope held to CP1 (preflight/health, two refusals, flextools_grammar_health).
plan.key_finding: The MCP server process never opens a FieldWorks project -- every OpenProject lives in the script text execution.py generates for the subprocess. That splits CP1 into reflection in-process and LCM reads in the subprocess, and makes SPEC 10.2 HC-agent probe unreachable from flextools_health (spec already rules skipped, not failed). Separately, SPEC 9.5.4 row 8 is refuted against the index.

T032 D-note) + US2 flextools_grammar_health(14, incl. the T016->T031->T029 research chain, T027 SPEC correction, T030 subprocess seam, T033 scan table) + US3 refusal helpers(4) + Polish(2); waves explicit with join lines, no [P] pair shares a file, US2 shares no file with US1/US3 so it ships standalone.

SPEC-5.4.title: ParserCore is gated by a capability probe -- same-install co-location plus a reflective member check -- never a version floor

SPEC-10.2.title: flextools_health grows a parser block with exactly two states per spine; one dead spine must not blank the other two

SPEC-14.title: Four additive error codes join tool-responses/1.0 with extra=forbid detail models, a TOOL-CONTRACT row each, and one CHANGELOG entry

SPEC-3.2.title: Never report the wrong engine's results as the project's -- ActiveParser is re-read live and a corrupt value reads as XAmple and refuses

SPEC-12.7.title: The HermitCrab agent may not exist; refuse with parser_agent_missing rather than let KeyNotFoundException escape, and leave the read spine ready

SPEC-9.5.5.title: flextools_grammar_health ships at CP1 -- pure LCM, READ_ONLY_SAFE, no export, no hc tool, no parse

SPEC-9.5.4.title: The pathology-to-LCM mapping is implemented in row order, every property name verified against the index first, with row 8 corrected and disabled rules excluded

SPEC-9.5.3.title: No scalar score, no grade, no ranking by magnitude -- size is anti-correlated with cost, so no field a client could sort on as a severity proxy

SPEC-9.5.7.title: A G4 finding names a suspect, never a defect -- report what was measured and what it costs, not that it is wrong

SPEC-3.1.title: Never infer parseability from database state -- the scan reads grammar objects only, never wordforms or analyses

SPEC-15.title: CP1 boundary: no parser is constructed, no grammar is loaded, nothing is parsed; HCParser is touched by reflection only

SPEC-H1.title: hc is a dotnet global tool located via PATH / dotnet tool list -g under a bounded timeout, never %LOCALAPPDATA%\HermitCrabTool\hc.dll

SPEC-10.1.title: next_step never proposes a tool that does not exist -- at CP1 the rows naming flextools_try_word degrade to tool: null, and the prose must not name it either

SPEC-16.title: The CP1-scoped verification groups all pass: envelope extra=forbid, ParserCore probe (5.4), HC agent probe (12.7), G4 grammar health (9.5), the two in-scope standing guarantees, and the Windows+FieldWorks no-hc integration bullet
